newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares rise 1.84 pct in limited recovery.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares rise 1.84 pct in limited recovery.

text.p: Istanbul shares regained part of Tuesday's sharp losses in a limited recovery on Wednesday, but fell from earlier highs amid caution due to ongoing political worries, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 27 points, or 1.84 percent higher at 1,492, but below a morning high of 1,516. It had plunged 6.98 percent yesterday on political worries and higher-than-expected January inflation data.
Trade volume firmed to 26.60 trillion lira ($227.2 million) from Tuesday's 22.79 trillion ($195.3 million).

"Political developments concerning the coalition government have unnerved the market although they are not seen strong enough to lead to a breakup in the coalition," said Hakan Aksoy from Alfa securities.

Reported uneasiness in the Islamist-led coalition's conservative wing over last Friday's Islamist protest and censure motions filed by two leftist parties against the government have depressed the market.
The index had lost 13.82 percent from last Monday's all-time high of 1,700 to Tuesday's close after surging 74.2 percent and hitting 17 record closes from end-1996 to January 27.

"Last month's strong uptrend seems to be over although the index may again rebound to 1,550-1,600 range. There won't be as strong a liquidity influx. Consolidation is normal after such a steep rally," said Aksoy.

Brokers said an approaching holiday also discouraged buying as Turkish investors mostly place their money in repo deals during long holidays. But some buying is awaited on Thursday and Friday because settlements will be delayed to after the holiday.
Turkish markets will be closed next Monday and Tuesday due to Islamic Ramadan holiday and will reopen on February 12.
